### Bisque (Paramount / TheSkyX)

Devices: Telescope.

Protocol documentation: `AlpacaCore/external/Bisque/` (INDI reference driver and TheSkyX scripting API docs). No external SDK required — communicates via JavaScript commands over TCP to TheSkyX Pro.

Connection types: TCP only. TheSkyX acts as middleware between the driver and the actual mount hardware.

- Communication is via JavaScript command snippets sent to the TheSkyX TCP scripting server (default port 3040).
- Commands are strings terminated with `#`. Responses are prefixed with `|No error. Error = 0.` on success, terminated with `#`.
- Special case: Handshake (`ConnectAndDoNotUnpark`/`IsConnected`) returns just `1` with no prefix.
- Slew is async: set `sky6RASCOMTele.Asynchronous = true`, call `SlewToRaDec`, poll `IsSlewComplete`.
- The 8 s Slewing hold after a slew command is `slew_hold_`, a `util::HoldWindow` ([decision 0022](../../docs/decisions/0022-hold-window.md), row `partial`, #1832): inside it the status poll and the retarget guard ask TheSkyX nothing, so an async slew's landing is seen no sooner than 8 s (the SlewToCoordinates wait polls `IsSlewComplete` itself); every read also needs `slewing_cached_`. Both slew forms arm it, with `slewing_cached_`, before `SlewToRaDec` goes out (`begin_slew_locked()`), and a `SlewToRaDec` TheSkyX refuses puts back the earlier slew's window, flag, kept poll error and `slew_claim_` (`undo_failed_slew_locked()`), so a SlewToCoordinates still waiting for that slew lowers Slewing when it lands. AbortSlew, connect, disconnect and the SlewToCoordinates wait's landing clear it. Tests: `[bisque][hold-window]`.
- Motion claims (#2263): `motion_owner_` (`util::MotionOwner`) holds them, under `mutex_`. A slew (`begin_slew_locked()`), Park and FindHome claim both axes and a non-zero MoveAxis its own; AbortSlew, Unpark and a disconnect or relink cancel both, `MoveAxis(axis, 0)` its own. TheSkyX runs every slew, park and home, so the driver's only bodies are the Park poll, the SlewToCoordinates wait and FindHome's IsSlewComplete poll: a Park or FindHome whose claim is no longer current writes neither `parked_`, `parking_` nor `at_home_`. Which slew owns `slewing_cached_` is `slew_claim_`, an owner claim the driver keeps, because a refused `SlewToRaDec` hands Slewing back to the earlier slew and the owner's generations only grow; AbortSlew empties it. PulseGuide during a slew or a FindHome is `InvalidOperation` ("PulseGuide is not allowed while a slew, park or home is running"), read from `slewing_cached_` and `homes_in_flight_` (counted from FindHome's gate to its every exit), not from `slew_running()`: the driver calls neither that nor `finished()`. A Park keeps its earlier `InvalidWhileParked`. PulseGuide on the axis a non-zero MoveAxis drives (North/South on Dec, axis 1; East/West on RA, axis 0) is `InvalidOperation` ("PulseGuide is not allowed on an axis MoveAxis is moving") and sends nothing, read from `manual_axis_slewing_` and `jog_pending_` (MoveAxis's gate to its every exit, over the open-loop start before its flag is set); the other axis is not checked (#2503). Pulses are not claimed: one DirectGuide holds the only socket, so a MoveAxis on either axis waits for its reply and the pulse ends on its own (`pulse_request_` still retires a guide on AbortSlew, connect and disconnect). Tests: `[bisque][motion-owner]`.
- Pulse guiding uses `sky6DirectGuide.MoveTelescope(dRA, dDec)` with arcsecond displacement. `sky6DirectGuide.lAsynchronous=0` makes that call wait for completion; keep it on a joinable driver worker so `PulseGuide()` returns promptly while `IsPulseGuiding` remains observable.
- Open loop motion for MoveAxis uses `DoCommand(9, 'direction|rate')` and `DoCommand(10, '')`.
- Park uses `ParkAndDoNotDisconnect()` to keep TCP connection alive (not `Park()` which disconnects).
- Pier side is read-only via `DoCommand(11, 'Pier Side')` — returns 1 for west of pier, else east.
- Find Home sends an asynchronous `FindHome()` and polls `IsSlewComplete` once a second for up to 60 seconds, so no exchange holds the link for the whole home and the status poll keeps publishing (a 60 s exchange would age the frame past `util::kLinkStalenessBound`). Only FindHome sets AtHome; every motion start clears it: the four equatorial slews (`note_slew_started_locked()`), MoveAxis at a nonzero rate, Park, PulseGuide and Tracking on (#2461).
- Slew speed presets: 9 rates (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 32x, 64x, 128x, 256x, 512x sidereal).
- UTCDate's source is the **TheSkyX computer**, never the bridge: Software Bisque's [Paramount ME II and MX User Guide](https://www.physics.muni.cz/~glos/Paramount/Paramount%20ME%20II%20and%20MX%20User%20Guide.pdf), pp. 27–29, requires Use Computer Clock and identifies that clock as the source for mount initialization and LST. [Script TheSky 1.32](https://www.bisque.com/wp-content/scriptthesky/index.html) executes ECMA-262 JavaScript remotely; `new Date().getTime()` supplies UTC milliseconds without timezone/DST conversion. In the same script, [DocumentProperty(5)/DocPropOut](https://www.bisque.com/wp-content/scriptthesky/classsky6_star_chart.html) must confirm UseComputerClock (nonzero). Manual/chart-time mode returns `InvalidOperation`; chart JD is not substituted. No script changes the clock mode, site, timezone or DST. Writes raise `PropertyNotImplemented` after connection/link checks: setting chart time is not setting the operating-system clock.
- The Script TheSky 1.32 `sky6StarChart::Sk6DocumentProperty` enum explicitly declares `sk6DocProp_UseComputerClock = 5`; its enumerator description says "Zero if not using the computers clock non-zero otherwise." See the [class reference](https://www.bisque.com/wp-content/scriptthesky/classsky6_star_chart.html), verified 2026-10-29. The fake does not establish this vendor fact.
- UTC is seeded at connect and refreshed by the existing status sample, with `UtcOffset` in the frame to advance remote UTC by task-clock elapsed time between replies. A failed time query retains the established anchor and records its diagnostic; without an anchor the getter raises that error. Explicit unavailable/manual mode clears the anchor. A later good reply re-anchors time. Snapshot resets and publication tokens prevent cross-session reuse. Stale alone does not refuse UTC; existing link fault/loss checks still apply. Evidence is fake-only (`[bisque][utcdate]`); actual TheSkyX script execution and hardware timing are not validated by the fake.
- Every TheSkyX exchange (connect and handshake, FindHome, Park and its polls, slews and their completion polls, sync, `SetTracking`, MoveAxis, Unpark, SetPark, the position samples at the end of sync, slew complete, FindHome and Park) runs with the driver `mutex_` free, under the protocol wrapper's per-link lock (the wrapper is one instance per process, so that lock is the I/O lock); `mutex_` stays the short state lock. MoveAxis, both slew forms and AbortSlew hold `initiator_mutex_` across gate, command and state write (a sync slew drops it before its wait); Park holds it across its gate and the Park send only, sets `parking_` before it lets go, and runs the IsParked poll without it, so a slew during the poll is refused like a parked mount and AbortSlew never waits for the poll (AbortSlew, Unpark and a disconnect clear `parking_` and cancel both axes on `motion_owner_` under `mutex_`, and a newer Park supersedes it; a Park whose claim is no longer current is retired: it returns quietly at its next poll boundary, writes neither `parked_` nor `parking_`, and the write after its last IsParked is gated on the claim too, so a cancelled or left-behind Park never sets `AtPark`, in this session or after a reconnect, #2062); both slew forms re-check Connected and park after the live IsTracking read; order `initiator_mutex_`, then the wrapper's lock, then `mutex_` (leaf). A control-path end takes the snapshot token under `mutex_`, samples without it and publishes under it, so a write since drops the publish (`publish_measurement()`). Connect runs under `transition_mutex_`; `set_connected(false)` clears state, releases `mutex_`, then closes the transport. Getters never wait behind the wire ([decision 0016](../../docs/decisions/0016-getters-never-wait-on-device-io.md)). Tests: the timing cases in `test_bisque_telescope_snapshot.cpp` (FindHome, SyncToCoordinates position read, `SetTracking`, the connect's IsParked query, Park's IsParked poll, a disconnect behind a PulseGuide reply, the sync slew's IsSlewComplete poll, the MoveAxis, SlewToCoordinatesAsync, Unpark and SetPark commands).
- **Motion fails closed** (#2410, the #2396 pattern; fake-only evidence, `[goto-safety]` cases in `test_bisque_telescope.cpp`). Each status poll tick first runs `enforce_motion_bounds()`: an async slew past `kMaxAsyncSlewDuration` (300 s from its `SlewToRaDec`, the synchronous wait excluded) gets a verified `Abort()`. The tick takes `initiator_mutex_` only with `try_lock`, so it never waits behind a motion command. A stop that worked logs at INFO (a client causes it, decision 0007 rule 9); one that failed logs WARN, keeps the motion flags and is tried again `kFailedStopRetry` (10 s) later. No start is ever re-sent. **The MoveAxis cap** (#2651) is not in the tick: each non-zero MoveAxis arms a `util::HoldWindow` of `util::kMaxMoveAxisDuration` (60 s) and starts a body in that axis's own slot (`move_axis_cap_[axis]`), which waits on the task clock and then runs `util::run_motion_deadline()`: `DoCommand(10)`, which stops both axes, sent under `initiator_mutex_` and verified by `IsSlewComplete` and two still position reads, up to 3 stops in all. A renewal, `MoveAxis(axis, 0)` and AbortSlew supersede the body (it checks its stop reason inside the initiator lock, so a body that woke while a newer rate command is on the wire sends nothing), and a disconnect joins it. A verified stop clears both axes' flags and Slewing raises "MoveAxis on axis N ran 60 s, the longest allowed; the driver stopped both axes" (INFO); a stop that does not verify keeps the flags and stores the failure (WARN) with no retry. Two MoveAxis calls on one axis start their bodies after the initiator lock is released, in either order: `start_move_axis_cap()` holds the axis's start lock and starts nothing for a window a newer move has replaced or a stop, AbortSlew or disconnect has cleared (`move_axis_cap_window_`), so an older body never replaces the newer move's cap. A start the slot refuses stops the axis and MoveAxis throws. Seams: `set_move_axis_cap_spawn_for_testing()`, `set_move_axis_cap_before_start_hook_for_testing()`. The synchronous wait's 120 s deadline sends the verified `Abort()` before it throws, unless a newer slew or an abort owns the mount (the wait's `util::MotionClaim` no longer owns Slewing, `owns_slewing_locked()`). AbortSlew also sends `DoCommand(10)` when a MoveAxis was running, and sends `Abort()` again while `IsSlewComplete` reads false, `kAbortRounds` (3) in all; a failed send or read ends the rounds. A failed or unverified AbortSlew puts back the motion flags it cleared. A `SlewToRaDec` with no reply or a failed send is unconfirmed (TheSkyX may have taken it): the driver stops the mount and the slew fails; a TheSkyX error reply (`is_theskyx_refusal()`) means nothing started. Each failure is stored in `motion_error_`, which Slewing raises and the synchronous wait checks before it treats a completion as a landing, until the next motion command (a slew, MoveAxis, AbortSlew, FindHome or Park) or a connect (`begin_motion_command_locked()`). Every stop that writes state after its exchange (the synchronous deadline, an unconfirmed slew, the poll's slew bound, AbortSlew) rechecks `session_` (bumped by every connect and disconnect) before it writes, so a disconnect and reconnect during its exchange keeps the new session clean (decision 0016 rule 6; seam `set_stop_sent_hook_for_testing`). A session that ends on a lost link with a slew or MoveAxis running leaves `relink_abort_pending_` (a slew) or `relink_move_stop_pending_` (a MoveAxis); the next connect sends the matching `Abort()` or `DoCommand(10)` right after the handshake, before any other command, and a stop that fails fails that connect and keeps the record. A client disconnect stops a running MoveAxis before the socket closes (a failed stop sets `relink_move_stop_pending_`); a GOTO is left to TheSkyX. Fake: `FakeBisqueMount::ignore_aborts`, `fail_abort`, `drop_slew_reply`, `reject_slew`, `fail_move_stop`, `ledger()`. Park's 120 s timeout sends the verified `Abort()` (TheSkyX's Park docs monitor a park with `IsSlewComplete`) unless a newer Park, an AbortSlew, an Unpark or a disconnect owns the mount (its Park claim retired, `parking_`), and rechecks `session_` before it writes. A stop that failed after a synchronous slew timeout, an unconfirmed slew or a Park timeout keeps Slewing true and is sent again by the poll `kFailedStopRetry` later (`retry_failed_slew_stop_locked()`, the reason kept in `slew_stop_reason_`). **Landing gate** (`util::LandingGate`, #2396 AB-7): after `IsSlewComplete` reads true, a slew is over only once two position reads `util::kStillSampleSpacing` apart agree; the synchronous wait reads every 500 ms, an async slew reads on each poll tick (so Slewing stays true about one tick longer). A mount at rest more than `util::kLandingFarMissArcsec` from its target fails the slew (`motion_error_`); each slew start arms its own gate (`landing_`), and a slew that ends with a stored failure (the driver had to stop it) is not landing-checked. The synchronous wait fails on a stored failure only when an AbortSlew or a retarget took the slew's claim (`owns_slewing_locked()`), so a MoveAxis failure during the wait does not fail the slew. A TheSkyX refusal is its own exception type in the wrapper (`TheSkyXRefusal`), not a message prefix. Fake: `abort_ends_park`, and a park in flight reads as a slew to `IsSlewComplete`.
- **Sync bound** (#2410): SyncToCoordinates is refused with InvalidValue (`util::check_sync_bound`, `util::kMaxSyncOffsetDegrees` = 5 deg on the sky) against the position the snapshot serves, before any command is sent. TheSkyX keeps its pointing model at power-up, as a handset does, so every Sync is bounded, the first after a connect included. The 5 deg bound and the 60 s MoveAxis cap are constants; per-device limits are out of scope here.
- The status poll is `util::PolledState<PolledFrame>` (`polled_`, decision 0010 rule 7, #2494): 1 s period, 3 s `max_age`, three failed ticks latch the fault, and the driver holds no `PolledLinkHealth`, poll slot or loss latch of its own; `link_lost_` is `polled_.link_lost()`, `get_link_fault()` is `polled_.fault()`, and loss closes the transport through the module's `on_lost` on the poll thread. The probe takes `polled_.begin_poll()` under `mutex_`, runs its exchanges without it, publishes with `polled_.publish()` under `mutex_` in the same hold that applies the `IsSlewComplete` outcome, and returns `nullopt`; a write since the token (abort, retarget, Tracking write) drops the frame and the outcome together. Control-path ends (sync, slew complete, FindHome, Park, pulse end) take the token under `mutex_`, sample without it and publish under it, through the same forwarders. A frame older than `max_age` is served as it is (stale never refuses); one no tick refreshed for `util::kLinkStalenessBound` is a lost link. The first probe of a connect seeds a frame with nothing known when TheSkyX is silent. PulseGuide is capped at 25 s (`kPulseGuideMaxMs`): the guide holds the wire for its duration plus 1 s and a frame is up to one period old at its start, so a longer pulse would read as a lost link at its end (a `static_assert` keeps the cap under the bound). Tests: `[bisque][snapshot][polled]`.
- **`findhomeissensorsearch` action**: false (`external_find_home`). A Paramount's TheSkyX Find Home is likely a homing-sensor search, but the driver cannot tell which mount TheSkyX drives and no Paramount run has verified it. Rule in [ascom-contract](ascom-contract.instructions.md#telescope-findhomeissensorsearch-action-every-telescope-driver).
